subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Gunpowder: Chemistry Meets Engineering
description: A quick, practical guide to Gunpowder: Chemistry Meets Engineering.

hook.text: Chinese alchemists searching for eternal life accidentally invented the most destructive substance on Earth.

buildup.text: Gunpowder mixes saltpeter, charcoal, and sulfur. The ratio determines if it burns or explodes.

discovery.text: China used it for fireworks and rockets. When it reached Europe, engineers built cannons.

twist.text: Cannons made castle walls obsolete overnight. Fortification engineering had to be reinvented completely.

climax.text: Star forts with angled walls replaced tall castles. Engineering adapted to the weapon it created.

punchline.text: The quest for immortality created the deadliest weapon.

quiz.question: How did gunpowder change fortification engineering?
options: It made walls thicker but the same height as before
It made tall castle walls obsolete, replaced by low star forts
It had no effect on building design, only on weapons
